players.product: electroplating chemistry for advanced packaging & substrates (MacDermid Alpha)

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q1 2026 (CFO): organic net sales grew 10% and constant currency adjusted EBITDA increased 21%; Electronics organic net sales grew 15%, the strongest in the segment since early 2021, with every vertical growing double-digits; under the new margin definition (excluding pass-through metals) adjusted EBITDA margin improved 170 basis points to 27.8%; adjusted EPS grew 21%. Q1 largely recovered the Q4 2025 tin/silver metals-hedge timing hit.
quarterly_data.figure: organic sales +10%; adj. EBITDA +21% cc; Electronics organic +15%; margin 27.8% (+170 basis points); adj. EPS +21%

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics verticals: Assembly Solutions grew 12% organically on sustained increases in high reliability alloys and engineered solder preforms sold to data center suppliers; Circuitry Solutions grew 17% organically from the high layer count server board market, with record quarterly sales in product categories tied to high-performance computing and AI server builds; Semiconductor Solutions grew 18% organically on improved power electronics order patterns, growing momentum in thermal interface products for AI GPU and CPUs, and strong and growing demand for advanced packaging solutions (magnified by higher precious metal prices).
quarterly_data.figure: Assembly +12% organic; Circuitry +17% organic; Semiconductor Solutions +18% organic

quarterly_data.signal: Acquisitions (both closed in Q1): Micromax (two months owned) contributed roughly $65 million to reported sales, roughly two-thirds metals-related, and grew double-digits organically; had Micromax been owned the full quarter, adjusted EBITDA would have been $170 million. EFC Gases & Advanced Materials contributed $19 million, a record first quarter, winning new semiconductor and space qualifications. Pass-through metals revenue was $256 million in Q1 2026 vs $101 million in Q4 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Micromax ~$65 million sales; EFC $19 million; pro forma adj. EBITDA $170 million; pass-through metals $256 million

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised (CEO): full-year adjusted EBITDA $665 million-$685 million, reflecting Q1 growth, continued electronics strength, softer industrial solutions and a less favorable FX tailwind; Q2 adjusted EBITDA $155 million-$170 million with demand sequentially similar to Q1 and some raw material/logistics inflation risk; 2026 adjusted EPS growth now high-teens. Confidence rests on durable data center demand through 2026 as the business shifts from consumer to longer-cycle enterprise applications.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adj. EBITDA $665 million-$685 million; Q2 $155 million-$170 million; adj. EPS growth high-teens

quarterly_data.signal: Capex raised: $25 million in Q1, trending above the prior $75 million annual run rate; now $75 million-$100 million for 2026 (still less than 3% of sales) for growth capex behind large commercial wins plus footprint consolidation. B2B customers' six to 12 month forecasts are rising rapidly (inaccurate in one direction), forcing a rethink of capacity; Kuprion investment is being accelerated, a few other product categories in the semi-assembly market need added capacity, and some engineered products have bottlenecks that need de-bottlenecking.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 capex $25 million; FY2026 capex $75 million-$100 million (less than 3% of sales)

quarterly_data.signal: Thermal materials: the company is seeing huge demand from hyperscalers for its thermal interface materials. Kuprion (copper as a substitute for silver) has a small handful of customers developing new applications; supply chain is the constraint, and investment is ramping to add capacity to serve those customers in 2027 and into 2028, with commercial activity limited so supply can keep up.

Market color (CEO): PCB growth will outstrip what was forecast entering the year (the circuitry business grew in the mid-teens this quarter); the smartphone-oriented business grew mid single-digits on high-end strength despite low-end weakness; the memory shortage accelerates the shift away from consumer electronics toward enterprise applications, with low-end PCBs most exposed to supply bottlenecks. Higher metal prices have caused no demand destruction and are pushing cash-strapped smaller competitors out of some markets; logistics/packaging inflation is tens of millions of dollars of unmitigated risk, mostly recoverable via surcharges.
